posts.title: Dua kata
posts.summary: Malam itu dingin. Sungguh dingin. Butiran salju terus mendarat di rambut pendekku. Keberadaannya seakan ingin menambah kesan berantakan padaku yang hanya mengenakan…

blocks.text: Oleh : Felicia Tiffany Hertada
blocks.en: By: Felicia Tiffany Hertada

blocks.text: Malam itu dingin. Sungguh dingin. Butiran salju terus mendarat di rambut pendekku. Keberadaannya seakan ingin menambah kesan berantakan padaku yang hanya mengenakan pakaian hari kemarin. Aku percaya rupaku pasti tak enak dipandang. Hingga semua orang hanya hilir mudik melewatiku. Sebentar saja mereka hanya melirik padaku. Walaupun ada beberapa yang berhenti mendengarkan aku bernyanyi bersama gitarku. Tetapi sedetik dua detik kemudian mereka pergi. Berhenti untuk iba mungkin? Melihat lelaki muda sepertiku bernyanyi tanpa suara.
blocks.en: The night was cold. Truly cold. Snowflakes kept landing in my short hair. As if they wanted to make me look even messier, wearing nothing but yesterday's clothes. I'm sure I wasn't nice to look at. So everyone just walked back and forth past me. Only for a moment did they glance my way. Though a few did stop to listen to me sing with my guitar. But a second or two later they left. Stopping out of pity, maybe? Seeing a young man like me singing without a voice.

blocks.text: Tapi tak apa, aku senang hanya dengan ini. Aku memang sebenarnya tak terlalu butuh perhatian. Aku disini, hanya untuk bernyanyi. Menyebarkan hobi anehku di setiap malam natal. Walaupun tiap tahun kota ini semakin sepi ditelan oleh kota lain yang lebih maju. Kemudian ketika malam itu hampir berakhir, aku menemukan gadis kecil menatapku dari kejauhan. Seorang gadis kecil berparas cantik usianya sekitar 10 tahun. Atau mungkin kurang dari itu. Tubuhnya tampak kedinginan. Telinganya ia biarkan terbuka hingga hanya warna merah yang terlihat. Padahal penutup telinga menggantung bosan di pergelangan tangan.
blocks.en: But that's fine, this alone makes me happy. I don't really need much attention anyway. I'm here only to sing. To spread my strange hobby every Christmas Eve. Even though every year this town grows quieter, swallowed by other, more advanced towns. Then, when the night was almost over, I found a little girl watching me from a distance. A pretty little girl, about 10 years old. Or maybe younger than that. She looked cold. She'd left her ears uncovered until all you could see was red. Even though her earmuffs dangled, bored, from her wrist.

blocks.text: Memang awalnya ia tidak kupedulikan. Kemudian seiring aku bernyanyi, ia masih setia melihat dari jauh. Kadang-kadang tersenyum. Kadang-kadang menatap kosong. Hingga aku mengemasi barangku tak lama kemudian. Tetapi ia tetap diam disitu seakan penasaran padaku. “Menarik” itu yang kupikirkan sejenak. Lalu aku pergi untuk pulang.
blocks.en: At first I didn't pay her any attention. Then, as I sang, she kept faithfully watching from afar. Sometimes smiling. Sometimes staring blankly. Until I packed up my things not long after. But she stayed still right there, as if curious about me. “Interesting” was what I thought for a moment. Then I left to go home.

blocks.text: Natal selanjutnya tetap dingin. Salju semakin banyak seiring dengan berkurangnya penduduk. Gitar favoritku menemani lagi malam ini. Malam dingin masih belum bisa mengalahkan rasa senangku setiap natal. Hari dimana aku bisa bebas. Hari dimana semua orang sibuk dengan orang tercinta dan tidak memperhatikanku. Lalu aku bernyanyi dan terus bernyanyi dalam diam dengan rasa puas. Malam hampir berakhir kembali dengan cepat. Kuperhatikan jalanan lagi sebelum pulang. Kulihat satu sisi dan sisi lainnya, kemudian aku terhenyak. Gadis kecil itu kembali. Tak tahu mengapa, ada rasa senang melihatnya kembali. Tetapi timbul juga penasaran.
blocks.en: The next Christmas was still cold. More and more snow as fewer and fewer people lived here. My favourite guitar kept me company again tonight. The cold night still couldn't beat the joy I feel every Christmas. The day I can be free. The day everyone is busy with their loved ones and doesn't notice me. So I sang and kept singing in silence, satisfied. The night was nearly over again, so fast. I looked over the street once more before going home. I looked one way and the other, and then I froze. The little girl was back. I don't know why, but I felt happy seeing her again. But curiosity rose too.

blocks.text: Penasaran akan dirinya. Gadis kecil yang setia menunggu dari jauh ketika orang lain tak acuh denganku. Ia tak maju, hanya diam di tempat. Seperti penguntit bisa dibilang. Tetapi sayang sekali. Ia datang terlambat. Malam hampir berakhir dan aku harus pulang. Memang sebenarnya tak tega melihatnya bersedih ketika aku berkemas. Lantas bagaimana lagi? Jika aku tak pulang, aku tak tahu apa yang akan mereka lakukan.
blocks.en: Curious about her. A little girl who waited faithfully from afar when everyone else didn't care about me. She didn't come closer, just stayed where she was. Like a stalker, you could say. But what a shame. She came too late. The night was almost over and I had to go home. Honestly, it hurt to see her sad as I packed up. But what else could I do? If I didn't go home, I didn't know what they would do.

blocks.text: Setahun lagi berlalu. Salju kembali melakukan tugasnya hari ini. Menemani natal untuk kesekian kalinya. Juga untuk menemani gadis kecil itu datang di akhir malam. Seperti biasa, tak sampai sepuluh menit ia datang dan aku terpaksa pulang meninggalkannya. Begitu pun natal selanjutnya, selanjutnya, dan selanjutnya. Walaupun terlambat, tiap tahun ia selalu datang. Kemudian melihat dari kejauhan. Ia tampak mendengarkan dan terkadang bergerak seakan mengikuti nada. Bahkan aku tahu ia pasti tak akan bisa mendengarku karena aku hanya bernyanyi dalam diam. Lalu mengapa ia begitu? Apakah untuk mengejekku? Mempermainkanku? Atau mungkin ia benar-benar mendengar suara hatiku bernyanyi? Membingungkan.
blocks.en: Another year went by. The snow did its job again today. Keeping Christmas company for who knows how many times. And keeping the little girl company as she came at the end of the night. As usual, not even ten minutes after she came, I had to go home and leave her. And the same the next Christmas, and the next, and the next. Late as she was, every year she always came. Then watched from a distance. She seemed to be listening and sometimes moved as if following the tune. Even though I knew she couldn't possibly hear me, because I only sang in silence. So why did she do that? To mock me? To toy with me? Or maybe she really could hear my heart singing? Confusing.

blocks.text: Tak sadar sebagian dariku telah menempatkan gadis kecil itu menjadi orang penting di hidupku. Walaupun aku hanya dapat melihatnya setiap natal dan dari kejauhan. Hanya dengan melihat tingkah anehya. Tetapi, aku pikir kami nyaman dengan itu.
blocks.en: Without realising it, part of me had made that little girl someone important in my life. Even though I could only see her every Christmas, and from a distance. Only by watching her strange little ways. But I think we were comfortable with that.

blocks.text: Sekali lagi malam natal tiba. Tak terasa keinginan bertemu gadis kecil itu telah menjadi tujuanku. Baru kali ini bernyanyi tak terlalu menjadi fokusku. Hingga kali ini aku datang lebih cepat dari biasanya. Padahal aku tahu ia akan tiba di akhir malam.
blocks.en: Once again Christmas Eve came. Without my noticing, wanting to see the little girl had become my reason for coming. For the first time, singing wasn't really my focus. So this time I came earlier than usual. Even though I knew she would only arrive at the end of the night.

blocks.text: “Ya mau bagaimana lagi, ia akan selalu datang terlambat. Atau mungkin nanti akan kucoba mendekatinya, ” kata hatiku.
blocks.en: “Well, what can I do, she'll always come late. Or maybe later I'll try going up to her,” my heart said.

blocks.text: Tetapi tak kusangka. Ketika matahari telah mengintip dan mengajak pulang salju, Ia masih belum muncul. Gadis kecil itu tak datang. Apakah benar ia tak datang? Setelah setia menemaniku setiap tahun? Aku masih tak percaya. Natal kali ini sungguh mengecewakan. Bahkan aku tak pulang untuk menunggunya. Memikirkan kekecewaan bagaimana aku tak pulang.
blocks.en: But I never expected it. When the sun had peeked out and invited the snow to go home, she still hadn't appeared. The little girl didn't come. Did she really not come? After faithfully keeping me company every year? I still couldn't believe it. This Christmas was truly disappointing. I didn't even go home, so I could wait for her. Thinking about my disappointment, how I hadn't gone home.

blocks.text: Hingga kemudian kata pulang membuatku terdiam. Terdiam dan teringat. Lalu meraih barangku dan berlari tak peduli. Bagaimana bisa aku lupa untuk pulang? Apa yang akan mereka lakukan jika aku tak pulang? Seketika itu, aku mulai melupakan peristiwa gadis kecil itu dan memikirkan tahun esok. Tahun yang akan berlalu sangat panjang.
blocks.en: Until the word home made me go still. Still, and remembering. Then I grabbed my things and ran, not caring about anything. How could I forget to go home? What would they do if I didn't go home? Right then, I started to forget about the little girl and think about the year ahead. A year that would pass very, very slowly.

blocks.text: Benar pemikiranku. Tahun ini terasa sungguh lama. Walaupun tidak seperti yang kuduga, Ini terasa lama bukan karena mereka. Tetapi karena gadis kecil itu. Aku tak bisa berhenti tentangnya. Apa yang terjadi padanya tahun lalu? Apakah ia terkena musibah dan jatuh sakit? Apakah ia terpaksa untuk pergi merantau? Atau mungkin yang terburuk terjadi, ia tak suka melihatku lagi? Segala kemungkinan muncul di otak kecilku. Lalu berhasil membuatku memutuskan untuk berhenti bernyanyi malam ini. Untuk mencari dirinya.
blocks.en: I was right. This year felt truly long. Though not the way I expected, it felt long not because of them. But because of the little girl. I couldn't stop thinking about her. What happened to her last year? Did something bad happen, did she fall ill? Was she forced to move away? Or maybe the worst had happened, she didn't like seeing me anymore? Every possibility popped into my little brain. And it got me to decide to stop singing tonight. To look for her.

blocks.text: Tekadku sudah bulat. Sayangnya, aku tak tahu harus memulai dari mana. Yang kutahu darinya hanyalah tempat dimana ia selalu menunggu, wajahnya, dan penutup telinga di tangannya. Sehingga saat ini aku hanya duduk diam di tempat itu. Di sebuah bangku kayu bersandar dibawah naungan lampu jalan. Lampu jalanan yang memancarkan cahaya kuning dan redup, tetapi menghangatkan.
blocks.en: My mind was made up. Sadly, I didn't know where to start. All I knew about her was the place where she always waited, her face, and the earmuffs on her wrist. So right now I just sat quietly in that spot. On a wooden bench with a backrest, under the shelter of a street lamp. A street lamp that gave off a dim yellow light, but a warm one.

blocks.text: Kutunggu ia datang. Menoleh kesana kemari . Berdiri berjalan kemudian duduk kembali. Semua usaha mencari kulakukan pada awalnya. Lalu tubuhku mulai kaku dingin seiring salju menutupi jalanan. Kulitku mulai memerah dingin bersamaan dengan berubahnya warna langit malam. Tetapi masih saja kutunggu ia datang.
blocks.en: I waited for her to come. Looking here and there. Standing, walking, then sitting back down. I tried everything to find her at first. Then my body began to go stiff with cold as the snow covered the street. My skin began to turn red with cold along with the changing colour of the night sky. But still I waited for her to come.

blocks.text: Lima jam sudah berlalu. Aku akhirnya menyerah. Ini sudah tengah malam dan ia belum datang. Lebih tepatnya tidak datang. Kuputuskan untuk pulang melewati jalan yang sudah sepi. Salju mengarakku berbelok di ujung gang. Kemudian sesuatu menabrakku. Napas tersengal-sengal terdengar. Kulihat objek tersangka penabrakku dan aku terhenyak.
blocks.en: Five hours had gone by. I finally gave up. It was already midnight and she hadn't come. Or, more precisely, wasn't coming. I decided to go home along the now-empty road. The snow paraded me around the corner at the end of the alley. Then something bumped into me. I heard ragged, panting breaths. I looked at the suspect who'd crashed into me and I froze.

blocks.text: Gadis kecil cantik itu berdiri di hadapanku. Tingginya hanya sepundakku dengan tubuh yang kurus. Senyumnya merekah melihatku tetapi ia tak bicara. Kita hanya terdiam bertatapan selama beberapa menit. Setelah itu ia meraih saku dan mengambil sebuah buku kecil bersampul bordir kayu. Ditulisnya sesuatu di bukunya itu kemudian memberikannya padaku.
blocks.en: The pretty little girl stood in front of me. She only came up to my shoulder, with a thin little body. Her smile bloomed when she saw me, but she didn't speak. We just stood silently looking at each other for a few minutes. After that she reached into her pocket and took out a small book with an embroidered wooden cover. She wrote something in her book and then handed it to me.

blocks.text: "Kenapa kakak tidak bernyanyi hari ini?" Begitu bunyi tulisannya. Lalu kutulis balik kepadanya tanpa bertanya mengapa ia tak bicara.
blocks.en: "Why didn't you sing today?" That was what it said. Then I wrote back to her without asking why she didn't speak.

blocks.text: "Untuk mencarimu gadis kecil. Aku sudah melihatmu sejak lama. Dimana kamu tahun lalu?" kuberikan padanya. Tetapi ia tak menjawab. Sepertinya aku salah bertanya. Kuambil lagi bukunya dan kutuliskan
blocks.en: "To look for you, little girl. I've been watching you for a long time. Where were you last year?" I handed it to her. But she didn't answer. Seems I asked the wrong question. I took her book again and wrote

blocks.text: " Ayo berkeliling kota bersamaku"
blocks.en: " Come walk around town with me"

blocks.text: Seketika itu matanya bersinar. Tangannya langsung menarikku ke arah tengah kota. Tempat dimana pesta natal diadakan. Ia berhasil membuat malam ini menjadi malam terbaikku. Malam dingin bersalju yang tidak kukira bisa menjadi seindah ini. Kami terus menikmati pesta bersama dan berkeliling kota. Dua putaran empat putaran, kami tidak peduli. Aku terlalu senang hingga melupakan untuk pulang. Kupikir gadis kecil ini juga merasakannya. Walaupun kami hanya berkomunikasi dengan tulisan dalam buku, kami puas sekali.
blocks.en: Right then her eyes lit up. Her hand pulled me straight toward the middle of town. Where the Christmas party was being held. She managed to make this night my best night ever. A cold, snowy night I never thought could be this beautiful. We kept enjoying the party together and wandering around town. Two rounds, four rounds, we didn't care. I was so happy I forgot to go home. I think this little girl felt it too. Even though we only talked through writing in the book, we were so content.

blocks.text: Rasa senang memang tak bisa lelah. Tetapi tubuh kami bisa. Ketika langit sudah mulai berubah warna, kami sudah bersantai kembali. Bersantai di bangku bersandar yang kami anggap milik kami. Lalu kulihat ia menulis dalam bukunya " Terimakasih untuk malam ini" bunyinya.
blocks.en: Happiness never gets tired. But our bodies do. When the sky began to change colour, we were relaxing again. Relaxing on the bench with the backrest that we thought of as ours. Then I saw her write in her book " Thank you for tonight" it said.

blocks.text: "Tentu, kita bisa melakukannya kembali tahun esok" Tetapi ia tak menjawab. Wajahnya tertunduk sedih ketika ia menulis.
blocks.en: "Of course, we can do it again next year" But she didn't answer. Her face drooped sadly as she wrote.

blocks.text: "Aku tak akan bisa. Panti asuhan akan memindahkanku ke kota lain besok " Aku tertegun. Menatapnya dengan lembut lalu menulis kembali.
blocks.en: "I can't. The orphanage is moving me to another town tomorrow " I was stunned. I looked at her gently, then wrote back.

blocks.text: "Benarkah itu?" Tanyaku dengan curiga karena aku tahu panti asuhan itu, satu-satunya panti asuhan di kota. Panti asuhan itulah yang mengirimku kepada mereka. Mereka yang mengadopsi dan memperbudak anak-anak panti. Aku tak ingin gadis kecil itu menjadi sepertiku. Bahkan mereka pasti telah menyiksanya selama ini. Berbagai kebencian muncul di dalam hatiku hingga tanpa sadar ia telah menulis kembali.
blocks.en: "Is that true?" I asked, suspicious, because I knew that orphanage, the only orphanage in town. That orphanage was the one that sent me to them. Them, who adopt the orphanage children and enslave them. I didn't want the little girl to end up like me. They must have been tormenting her all this time too. All kinds of hatred welled up in my heart, until without my noticing she had written again.

blocks.text: "Benar, aku sukarela menggantikan temanku satu-satunya untuk dikirim kesana dan itulah yang mencegahku kesini tahun lalu" kalimat itu membuatku sungguh terkesima padanya. Tetapi sekaligus ada rasa bersedih untuknya.
blocks.en: "Yes, I volunteered to take the place of my only friend to be sent there, and that's what kept me from coming here last year" That sentence left me truly in awe of her. But at the same time I felt sad for her.

blocks.text: "Berarti kau tahu apa yang akan dilakukan panti itu?"
blocks.en: "So you know what that orphanage is going to do?"

blocks.text: Ia tersenyum dan mengangguk. Akhirnya aku memutuskan untuk bercerita padanya tentang diriku yang pernah menjadi anak dari panti asuhan itu. Tetapi di akhir cerita, ia menangis. Itu membuat orang-orang dari kedai di pinggir jalan memperhatikan kami sejenak. Lalu kembali ke kegiatan utama mereka. Aku sibuk menenangkan gadis itu.
blocks.en: She smiled and nodded. In the end I decided to tell her about myself, how I was once a child of that orphanage. But at the end of the story, she cried. That made the people at the stalls by the roadside look at us for a moment. Then they went back to what they were doing. I was busy trying to calm the girl down.

blocks.text: "Mengapa kau menangis?" Tulisku dalam buku kecilnya. Kemudian ia mengelap air matanya dan menulis.
blocks.en: "Why are you crying?" I wrote in her little book. Then she wiped her tears and wrote.

blocks.text: "Kamu pasti sungguh sedih" Dia bersedih untukku? Bagaimana dengan dirinya?
blocks.en: "You must be so sad" She was sad for me? What about herself?

blocks.text: "Tidakkah kau sedih karena harus pergi kesana?"
blocks.en: "Aren't you sad that you have to go there?"

blocks.text: "Tidak, kamu sudah mengalaminya. Tetapi aku belum tahu apa yang akan terjadi."
blocks.en: "No, you've already been through it. But I don't know yet what will happen."

blocks.text: Kemudian aku berpikir. Berpikir tentang bagaimana caraku untuk membuatnya tidak menderita dengan mereka.
blocks.en: Then I thought. Thought about how I could keep her from suffering with them.

blocks.text: Pagi itu, saat itu juga aku melamun lumayan lama. Ia bersabar menungguku sambil menikmati proses bangunnya sang surya. Setelah satu jam berlalu, aku rebut bukunya menghasilkan gadis kecil yang terkejut. Semua kemungkinan sudah kupikirkan dan inilah satu-satunya jalan. Aku tulis kemungkinan itu di bukunya.
blocks.en: That morning, right then, I was lost in thought for quite a while. She waited patiently for me, enjoying the sun as it woke up. After an hour had passed, I snatched her book, leaving the little girl startled. I'd thought through every possibility and this was the only way. I wrote that possibility in her book.

blocks.text: "Ayo pergi bersamaku." Ia membacanya dan menoleh kepadaku. Dengan perlahan ia menulis.
blocks.en: "Come away with me." She read it and turned to me. Slowly she wrote.

blocks.text: "Bolehkah?"
blocks.en: "Can I?"

blocks.text: Memang aku tampak sangat tidak meyakinkan. Tetapi pilihan ini telah kuperhitungkan. Bahkan perhitunganku mampu untuk membuatku berdiri dengan mantap. Lalu menjulurkan tanganku dan mengajaknya. Seperti yang kuharapkan, tangannya perlahan-perlahan mulai meraihku. Tetapi ia berhenti di tengah seakan ada sesuatu yang mencegahnya. Ia mengembalikan tangannya untuk meraih buku dan menulis.
blocks.en: Sure, I looked very unconvincing. But I had already weighed this choice. My weighing even let me stand up firmly. Then I held out my hand and asked her to come. Just as I hoped, her hand slowly, slowly began to reach for mine. But she stopped halfway, as if something were holding her back. She drew her hand back to reach for the book and wrote.

blocks.text: "Tetapi...aku tuli"
blocks.en: "But...I'm deaf"

blocks.text: Kata kata itu menyadarkanku dan membuatku berpikir lebih cepat. Tentang bagaimana ia tak mau bicara, hanya menulis, dan tak tahu suara sekitar. Semua masuk akal jika dihubungkan. Walaupun begitu, itu tidak mencegahku.
blocks.en: Those words woke me up and made me think faster. About how she wouldn't speak, only wrote, and didn't know the sounds around her. It all made sense once you put it together. Even so, it didn't stop me.

blocks.text: Kuraih tangannya dan mengambil bukunya. Kemudian membuka pulpen dengan perlahan. Semua terasa berhenti saat aku menulis. Gadis kecil ini memandangku penuh harapan sekaligus tegang. Aku serahkan kembali padanya buku itu. Matanya bergerak membaca tulisanku. Setelah itu, matanya bergerak melihatku dengan senyuman di wajahnya. Lalu kali ini ia yang menggandeng tanganku. Kami berlari kabur dari kota ini dan sejak saat itu hidup kami berubah. Sejak saat aku menuliskan dua kata itu di bukunya. Dua kata “aku bisu”.
blocks.en: I took her hand and took her book. Then slowly uncapped the pen. Everything felt like it stopped while I wrote. This little girl looked at me, full of hope and nervous all at once. I handed the book back to her. Her eyes moved, reading my writing. After that, her eyes moved to look at me with a smile on her face. And this time she was the one who took my hand. We ran away from this town and from then on our lives changed. Ever since I wrote those two words in her book. Two words: “I'm mute”.

blocks.text: Oleh : Felicia Tiffany Hertada
blocks.en: By: Felicia Tiffany Hertada

blocks.text:
Perdebatan itu terjadi di lorong kecil berlukiskan semburat-semburat cahaya jingga. Dengan pola bergaris, mereka mengintip dan mencetak ventilasi ruangan yang kedap dan lembap sebelum digantikan sang rembulan. Walau begitu, ruangan ini tetap penuh kunjungan manusia-manusia yang memikul bajunya masing-masing. Satu orang membawa baju-baju yang semerbak busuk baunya dan yang lain keluar berbekal wangi raut muka yang puas. Siapakah mahasiswa yang tidak memilih untuk menghabiskan waktu senggang ini untuk mendaur ulang busana mereka? Berburu saling menunggu giliran untuk berkesempatan mencuci busana mereka.
Namun, di balik itu, jumlah antrean ini sudah terlewat batas normal. Mahasiswa- mahasiswi ini seperti telah gila mencuci dan bergaya dengan busananya yang terus berganti. Baru saja sela-sela perubahan jam kelas, masing-masing dari mereka telah rajin mengganti model bajunya. Ada yang berkata, “sudah basi model baju ini aku gunakan berjam-jam” dan sisanya tidak dapat memberi alasan selain “bukankah ini normal?”
Konon katanya semua ini bermula sekitar 10 tahun lalu. Terkisahkan seorang mahasiswa yang baru memasuki tahun pertama di kampus itu. Awalnya tak ada yang tahu siapakah dirinya. Hingga orang-orang mulai memperhatikan dan tertarik dengan dirinya. Tiap- tiap hari ia gunakan busana yang berbeda namun terlihat sangat mewah. Ke mana pun ia pergi, semua orang di kampus itu mengenalnya. Tak pernah sekalipun orang-orang melihat dirinya menggunakan baju yang sama. Setiap hari merek baju terkenal dan mahal bergantian melekat di tubuhnya. Tanpa tahu apa-apa semua orang mengenalnya dengan julukan si kaya.
Si kaya ini kemudian mendapat julukan lain yaitu si jenius. Semua nilai-nilai di atas kertas sangat sempurna. Apalagi kehidupan sosialnya yang tak membosankan. Anehnya tak ada yang menyadari bahwa semakin terkenal dirinya, semakin meningkat prestasinya. Sebagaimana tak ada yang menyadari bahwa dirinya dulu hanya mahasiswa biasa. Namun semakin terkenal dirinya, semakin banyak pengajar yang memberikannya hak-hak istimewa agar diakui oleh mahasiswa itu. Semakin banyak orang-orang yang peduli kepadanya dan baik padanya. Si kaya dan jenius kini menjadi bintang di kampus itu.
Tren-tren busana di kampus kini mulai mengikuti model sang kaya dan jenius. Mahasiswa-mahasiswi hingga keluarga di kampus itu juga mulai menjadikannya teladan. Si kaya dan jenius juga sadar dirinya menjadi bintang di kampus dan ia memanfaatkan hal itu.

The debate took place in a small corridor painted with streaks of orange light. In striped patterns, they peeked in and printed themselves on the vents of the airtight, humid room before the moon took their place. Even so, the room stayed full of people, each one carrying their own clothes. One came in with clothes that reeked of rot and another walked out wearing the fragrance of a satisfied face. Which student wouldn't choose to spend their free time recycling their clothes? Hunting, waiting for each other's turn, for a chance to wash their clothes.
But behind all that, the queue had gone past normal limits. These students seemed to have gone mad over washing and showing off clothes that kept changing. In the short gaps between classes, every one of them had dutifully changed outfits. Some said, “this outfit's gone stale, I've worn it for hours” and the rest could give no reason other than “isn't this normal?”
Legend has it that all of this began about 10 years ago. The story goes of a student who had just started his first year at that campus. At first nobody knew who he was. Until people began to notice him and grew interested in him. Every single day he wore different clothes, and they looked so luxurious. Wherever he went, everyone on campus knew him. Not once did people see him wear the same clothes twice. Every day famous, expensive brands took turns clinging to his body. Without knowing a thing about him, everyone knew him by the nickname the rich one.
The rich one then got another nickname: the genius. All his grades on paper were perfect. Not to mention his social life, which was never boring. Strangely, no one noticed that the more famous he became, the more his achievements rose. Just as no one noticed that he used to be only an ordinary student. But the more famous he became, the more teachers gave him special privileges so he would acknowledge them. The more people cared about him and were kind to him. The rich genius was now the star of that campus.
Fashion trends on campus began to follow the rich genius's style. Students, and even the families on that campus, began to make him their role model. The rich genius knew he had become the campus star, and he took advantage of it.

Banyak orang yang sudah meminta saran kepadanya, tentang bagaimana caranya menjadi bintang, namun ia hanya menjawab.
“Orang-orang hanya melihat dirimu dari penanmpilan luarmu saja. Jadi kau tahu apa yang harus kamu lakukan.” Begitulah bagaimana kegilaan berbusana di sekolah itu dimulai. Orang-orang berburu untuk membeli baju dan menunjukkan eksistensi mereka. Tak sedikit pula yang membeli barang-barang palsu hanya untuk meningkatkan namanya di kalangan publik. Sehingga pada akhirnya semua kegilaan ini menjadi hal normal di kampus itu.
Kini, si kaya dan jenius sudah menjadi alumni kenangan di kampus itu. Sebagai seorang alumni yang menjadi ikon kampus. Orang-orang kini menyebutnya presiden busana. Seperti mengguncang dunia, presiden busana kini telah meninggalkan jejaknya di kampus itu dengan sistem tak kasat mata ini.
Maka dari itu, mahasiswa di kampus busana, yang memang kampus ini diberi nama itu, mulai berfokus pada penampilan dibanding kebutuhan untuk mengejar ilmu. Busana dan nama baik diutamakan di atas buku-buku dan medali logam. Mengetahui hal ini, kampus mulai membuat kebijakan baru. Mulai saat ini juga, tidak ada yang disebut dengan nilai dan peringkat. Tetapi nilai digeserkan dengan kebebasan menggunakan busana. Semakin tinggi prestasi dan nilai seorang mahasiswa, semakin bebas jenis busana yang dapat mereka gunakan. Maka dari itu, peringkat-peringkat mahasiswa dapat semua orang lihat dengan caranya berbusana.
Namun tak disangka, sistem ini kemudian berjalan hingga puluhan tahun umur kampus. Tidak ada pihak-pihak yang berusaha mengkritik. Dibiarkan begitu saja. Seakan-akan sistem ini tidak memiliki lubang di mana pun. Walaupun, mahasiswa kini saling berusaha menjatuhkan dan mencari nilai hanya untuk kebutuhan penampilan. Lalu, apakah lembaga pendidikan salah menilai? Atau kritikan dibungkam hanya untuk menjadi dongeng pengantar tidur?
Di antara alumni kampus busana, ada satu mahasiswa yang merebut kebebasan berbusana peringkat atas di hari pengumuman kelulusan. Terlihat dirinya tidak pernah memegang buku ataupun menyentuh buku untuk hanya menerawang halaman demi halaman. Tidak hanya untuk prestasi akademik, ia juga selalu menjuarai olimpiade olahraga yang ia ikuti. Mahasiswa lainnya hanya bisa menyebutnya si peramal. Bagaikan ia tahu seperti apa soal-soal ujian yang keluar ataupun merancang strategi untuk permainan fisik. Kata teman- temannya, di awal semester, nilainya tak pernah sebagus ini. Hingga suatu hari ia bertindak aneh dan mencurigakan. Tidak lewat satu minggu, ia kembali bertindak normal. Namun, busananya menjadi sangat mewah dan seketika ia menjadi idola banyak wanita. Tetapi tidak ada yang tahu. Bagaimana rahasia si peramal memenangkan semua ini dan mendapatkan kebebasan berbusana hanya dalam waktu beberapa hari.
Sebenarnya, si peramal hanya pandai berolahraga. Namun, pihak kampus busana tak menganggap prestasi dan bakat ini sebagai sebuah prestasi yang wajib dianggap. Berbusana yang anggun layaknya digunakan untuk kegiatan yang berwibawa, bukannya berlompat- lompat dan berlari dalam sebuah kompetisi olahraga. Makin pusinglah ia karena kehidupan kampusnya kian sulit. Hampir semua orang yang ia temui meremehkannya karena bajunya yang selalu bau dan kusut akibat ia rajun berlatih. Dulu, nilai biasa pun tak apa, busana minimalis pun ia tak apa. Sebesar itulah pengaruh busana terhadap perlakuan orang kepadanya. Hingga ia yang lelah pun mencari cara untuk mendapatkan nilai terbaik. Begitulah mengapa setiap sehari atau dua hari sebelum ujian dimulai, si peramal selalu menyelinap ke ruang berkas sekolah. Dengan bakatnya, ia dapat dengan mudah mendapatkan kunci jawaban untuk semua soal ujian.
Hal ini terjadi selama beberapa tahun ia bersekolah. Hingga tanpa disadari, sebuah organisasi gelap untuk transaksi kunci jawaban semakin merajalela di kampus. Mahasiswa- mahasiswi berbahagia karena mereka kini tak perlu bersusah payah mendapatkan hak istimewa berbusana. Mereka semakin malas dan memberikan kepercayaan mereka untuk ujian kepada si peramal. Jumlah busana yang digunakan mahasiswa untuk nama baik mereka meningkat drastis. Organisasi yang ditutupi dengan nama pendekar ketertiban berbusana itu semakin meluas tanpa sepengetahuan kampus. Antara tak tahu atau pura-pura tak tahu untuk menjaga reputasi kampus. Hingga ia pun kini menjadi alumni yang dicari-cari orang. Karena prestasinya, bukan perbuatan buruknya. Walau begitu, tidak tenang hatinya karena kegelisahan dan rasa takut. Bagaimana jika dirinya mengecewakan dan diinjak-injak kembali? Bagaimana jika orang-orang tahu akan rahasianya dan ia akan kembali ke masa lalunya dengan busana yang tak bernilai?
Rasa gelisah itu terus menggerogoti hatinya. Tiap-tiap hari ia menolak tawaran jabatan dengan alasan menikmati masa kelulusan terlebih dahulu. Pada akhirnya, ketika hartanya telah habis, ia memilih untuk mencuri dengan bakatnya. Karena hanya itulah yang bisa ia lakukan dan pelajari selama menempuh pendidikan. Semua hal yang ia kejar demi penampilan dan busana kini tak ada artinya. Lima tahun berlalu dan konon katanya sebuah grup mafia baru telah menjadi kriminal nomor satu dalam negeri.
Di tahun selanjutnya, sistem pendidikan di kampus diubah. Penilaian tidak berdasarkan atas kunci jawaban pasti namun jawaban-jawaban esai yang diinginkan guru. Nilai yang diatas rata-rata makin sulit didapatkan dan kampus mulai kembali ke zaman sebelum presiden busana datang. Seketika tak ada yang superior dalam berbusana. Seketika tak ada lagi kunci jawaban untuk diselundupkan dan nilai siswa turun dengan tajam. Walau begitu, di dalam sistem apapun, akan tetap ada yang berada di atas. Ia adalah seorang mahasiswi jenius yang menjuarai sejuta esai dalam negeri. Putri esai katanya. Bagai tak ada habisnya, ide selalu ia dapatkan untuk kembali menulis, menulis, dan berkarya. Ia selalu terlihat bekerja di depan kertas-kertas ataupun mesin ketik modern. Semua esainya seperti jendela-jendela dunia yang mencakup semua ilmu. Banyak yang berkata sejak kecil ia sudah membaca ribuan buku. Ada pula yang berkata bahwa orang tuanya mulai mendidiknya ilmu eksak sejak balita. Rumor-rumor itu terus berputar dibelakangnya yang tak sadar karena terlalu sibuk menulis.
Andai saja ada yang tahu siapakah ia sebenarnya. Sebelum masuk ke kampus ini, ia adalah seorang artis fesyen di majalah-majalah besar. Kehidupannya telah berputar mengenai busana-busana dan hidup seakan tak bermakna tanpa adanya pujaan orang lain. Kemudian paniklah ia ketika memasuki kampus busana. Berbagai cara ia coba dan akhirnya gelar putri esai ia dapatkan. Ia pun kini lulus dengan nilai terbaik di seluruhh penjuru negeri.
Putri esai sudah memiliki pengikut dari seluruh dunia. Bagaimana tidak? Ia yang awalnya adalah seorang artis, kini ditambah dengan keunggulan bakatnya dalam menulis. Karena itu, akhirnya sang putri memutuskan untuk melanjutkan karirnya dalam menulis untuk publik. Buku demi buku ia terbitkan. Bahasan dimulai dari politik hingga ilmu pengetahuan tak terlewatkan.
Dibalik banyaknya penggemar bermunculan, spam surel dari oknum tak dikenal semakin menumpuk. Tahu akan isinya, sang putri semakin berniat mengabaikannya. Begitu juga pihak seberang, semakin tak terjawab surel mereka, semakin besar pula niat mereka mendatangi sang putri esai. Hingga akhirnya rumah sang putri didobrak dengan keras dan sang putri ditangkap atas dugaan keras melakukan plagiarisme. Ribuan rumor tentang buku yang ia baca. Namun kenyataannya ribuan jurnal yang ia tiru. Kini semua itu berubah menjadi ribuan hari dalam kurungan. Konon katanya, di dalam jeruji penjara ia semakin gila karena dirinya tak memiliki pendirian. Ia merasakan hidupnya hampa karena tak ada lagi yang dapat ia tiru. Dirinya pun memutuskan untuk mengakhiri hidupnya dalam jeruji yang kosong akan pujian- pujian dari penggemarnya.
Kedua alumni yang telah lulus terkena kasus. Mahasiswa dan mahasiswi tak tahu akan hal ini. Mereka terlalu sibuk mengejar hak istimewa untuk berpenampilan yang terbaik dan mendapatkan pelayanan terhormat dari orang lain. Nilai dan pendidikan dikejar-kejar dengan tujuan yang salah. Beginilah prosedur yang mereka tahu. Mencari cara mendapatkan angka-angka yang tinggi kemudian berbusana, bukan untuk mengejar mimpi. Serendah itukah kodrat sebuah mimpi?
Selain mencari nilai dan memperbaiki penampilan luar, ada hal lain yang mereka pelajari. Seperti pentingnya sebuah koneksi dan hak-hak istimewa. Tidak belajar dari keadaan, banyak anak yang kemudian berusaha dekat dengan pengajar demi mendapatkan angka-angka diatas kertas yang sempurna. Namun mereka lakukan ini dengan merendahkan derajat guru melalui tawaran harta. Suapan dan sogokan uang berkali-kali lipat menjadi tren terbaru di sekolah ini. Hingga beberapa mahasiswa lain yang mengetahui fakta ini menganggapnya sebagai hal normal dan tidak menceritakannya kepada orang lain. Mereka kira mahasiswa ini, sebut saja para kontraktor, memang berhak mendapatkannya. Begitulah masalah ini menjadi rahasia umum yang tidak pernah dibantah siapapun.
Walau begitu, tidak bisa dikata untung atau sayang. Tidak semua siswa berlatar belakang bagus dan tinggi. Itulah mengapa, anak berandal, pembolos, dan pemalas dapat berbusana tanpa adat dan sangat bebas. Busana menjadi alasan untuk berbisnis buruk dan politik yang kotor. Kembali kita berkata. Konyol sekali.
Ketika mahasiswa-mahasiswi melupakan tidur mereka untuk saling menjatuhkan yang lain dengan angka-angka ilusi dalam laporan pendidikan, para kontraktor itu mendapat fasilitas penuh di kampus. Hidupnya sangat tenang. Begitu naifnya sampai-sampai mereka tak tahu solusi dalam segala persoalan hidup selain dengan harta. Sejak kecil, mereka hanya perlu melakukan yang diperintahkan orang tuanya dan mendapat upah untuk dihabiskan. Sehingga, ketika kertas-kertas motivasi mahasiswa-mahasiswi lain berisi daftar busana yang akan mereka beli, hanya kertas mereka yang berlukiskan menara Eiffel dan bangunan-bangunan tinggi di Amerika. Tentunya hal ini atas perintah orang tuanya pula. Miris sekali.
Tapi memang benar, mimpi mereka tercapai. mereka meraihnya seperti kuda. Mereka dapat pergi ke negeri-negeri tetangga hanya sebagai tunggangan. Sebagai alat untuk dikendalikan karena hartanya berlimpah namun otaknya kosong. Bahagia dalam kebodohannya sendiri. Orang pertama dari mereka memasuki ruang kerjanya, menandatangani surat-surat, dan pulang ke rumah. Hartanya terus masuk dan satu tahun itu berjalan dengan lancar. Hingga suatu hari, sekelompok kriminal menemuinya diam-diam. Surat-surat yang selama ini ia tanda tangani ternyata adalah surat-surat hutang dengan kelompok kriminal itu. Hari itu, seorang kontraktor hilang tanpa kabar. Keluarganya sadar mereka tak bisa apa-apa dan hanya bisa berharap. Konon katanya, teriakan mengerikan selalu terdengar setiap malam di tempat terakhir dirinya terlihat. Semakin lama, semakin keras suara itu. “Itu bukan aku. Aku tak tahu apa-apa!” begitulah teriakan berbunyi setiap malam. Ketidaktahuan melahap dirinya sendiri.
Cerita sang kontraktor lain juga berakhir buruk. Sama seperti nasib orang pertama, mereka lulus tanpa membawa apa-apa. Tidak ada prestasi, tidak ada nilai, tidak ada masa depan. Setiap hari mereka hanya menjadi lintah untuk orang tua mereka. Beberapa memilih untuk mengulang jenjang pendidikan mereka. Beberapa yang lainnya lanjut bekerja dan mendapat jabatan atas nama uang. Begitulah hidup mereka tidak berguna dan hanya menjadi busuknya sampah masyarakat. Hidup bersama lintah yang lain, hanya menjadi pemuja untuk nama baik, penampilan, dan harta yang terus berputar di antara mereka.
Adanya kasus-kasus mahasiswa ini pun dikubur oleh kampus dengan bungkaman kertas-kertas bertinta dolar. Peraturan busana semakin didewakan dan tak ada upaya menghilangkan diskriminasi busana di sini. Lalu, siapakah yang tidak menjadi gila dan jahat disini? Tidak normal sekali dirinya. Tapi memang ada.
Mahasiswa itu adalah juara dalam segala bidang. Olahraga ia juarai dan menjadi yang tercepat. Seni yang subjektif seakan dibaca olehnya. Sastranya menggerakkan hati semua orang. Tidak selesai ia berprestasi, ilmu-ilmu eksak pun ia hafalkan di luar kepala. Organisasi dalam kampus ia ketuai dengan handal. Sepertinya, tak ada yang ia tak bisa lakukan di dunia ini.
Kepintarannya itu di sisi lain mengundang kelicikan dan ego yang tinggi baginya. Setiap hari dirinya berubah busana. Sang bertalenta melihat keadaan ini sebagai keuntungan yang dapat dimanfaatkan. Suatu hari, ia gunakan baju tim olimpiadenya untuk mendapatkan fasilitas-fasilitas olahraga tanpa membayar. Lain hari, diam-diam ia gunakan medalinya untuk mencuri buku- buku di perpustakaan dengan mengatasnamakan pihak perlombaan. Keesokan harinya lagi, ia gunakan jaket organisasi untuk alasan telat dan membolos saat kuliah berlangsung. Begitu terus setiap hari tipuannya selalu berubah agar tidak diketahui.
Hingga di hari kelulusannya, ia puas dan mendapat pekerjaan di salah satu perusahaan terkenal di dunia. Walau begitu pangkatnya tak cukup tinggi di sana. Untuk naik pangkat pun ia tak bisa. Otak yang cerdas tidak cukup baginya karena atasannya selalu memanfaatkan kejeniusannya itu. Setiap ide jenius yang ia ajukan selalu diklaim dan semua kesalahan dijatuhkan kepadanya. Ada baiknya dirinya pintar karena si bertalenta ini dapat bertahan hingga saat ini. Namun, karena itu pula penderitaannya bertahan lama. Waktu demi waktu berganti, hingga hari tua ia bertahan pada jabatan itu dan tidak dapat berpindah kerja. Begitulah bagaimana si bertalenta mendapatkan karmanya, dengan dimanfaatkan.

Many people had asked him for advice, about how to become a star, but he only answered.
“People only see you by your outward appearance. So you know what you have to do.” That's how the fashion madness at that school began. People hunted for clothes to buy and to show off their existence. Quite a few even bought fake goods just to raise their name in public. So in the end all this madness became something normal on that campus.
Now, the rich genius has become a fond memory of an alumnus on that campus. An alumnus who became the campus icon. People now call him the fashion president. As if he had shaken the world, the fashion president has left his mark on that campus with this invisible system.
And so, the students at the fashion campus, which really is what this campus is called, began to focus on appearance rather than on the need to pursue knowledge. Clothes and good names came before books and metal medals. Knowing this, the campus began to make a new policy. Starting right now, there is no such thing as grades and rankings. Instead, grades were replaced with the freedom to wear clothes. The higher a student's achievements and grades, the freer the kind of clothes they could wear. And so, everyone could see a student's ranking by the way they dressed.
But unexpectedly, this system went on to run for decades of the campus's life. No one tried to criticise it. It was just left alone. As if this system didn't have a single hole anywhere. Even though students now try to bring each other down and chase grades only for the sake of appearance. So, did the educational institution judge wrongly? Or was criticism silenced just to become a bedtime story?
Among the alumni of the fashion campus, there was one student who seized the top-ranked freedom of dress on graduation announcement day. He never seemed to hold a book, or even touch one just to skim page after page. Not only in academics, he also always won the sports olympiads he entered. The other students could only call him the fortune teller. As if he knew what the exam questions would be, or how to plan his strategy for physical games. According to his friends, at the start of the semester his grades were never this good. Until one day he acted strange and suspicious. Not even a week passed and he was back to acting normal. But his clothes became very luxurious and instantly he became the idol of many women. Yet nobody knew. What the fortune teller's secret was to winning all this and getting freedom of dress in just a few days.
Actually, the fortune teller was only good at sports. But the fashion campus didn't consider this achievement and talent an achievement worth counting. Elegant dress was meant for dignified activities, not for jumping and running around in a sports competition. His head spun even more as his campus life got harder and harder. Almost everyone he met looked down on him because his clothes were always smelly and wrinkled from all his training. Back then, ordinary grades were fine, and minimalist clothes were fine with him too. That's how big the influence of clothes was on how people treated him. Until, worn out, he looked for a way to get the best grades. That's why, one or two days before every exam, the fortune teller always snuck into the school's records room. With his talent, he could easily get the answer keys for every exam.
This went on for the several years he was at school. Until, without anyone realising, a dark organisation trading answer keys ran rampant on campus. The students were happy because they no longer had to struggle to earn the privilege of dress. They grew lazier and handed their trust for exams to the fortune teller. The amount of clothes students wore for the sake of their good names rose drastically. The organisation, hidden behind the name the guardians of dress order, kept spreading without the campus knowing. Either not knowing or pretending not to know, to protect the campus's reputation. Until he too became an alumnus everyone was looking for. Because of his achievements, not his bad deeds. Even so, his heart was never at peace, because of the worry and the fear. What if he disappointed everyone and got trampled on again? What if people found out his secret and he went back to his past, with clothes worth nothing?
That anxiety kept gnawing at his heart. Day after day he turned down job offers, saying he wanted to enjoy life after graduation first. In the end, when his money ran out, he chose to steal with his talent. Because that was the only thing he could do and had learned in all his years of education. Everything he had chased for appearance and clothes now meant nothing. Five years passed and legend has it that a new mafia group had become the country's number one criminals.
The following year, the education system on campus was changed. Grading was no longer based on fixed answer keys but on the essay answers the teachers wanted. Above-average grades got harder to get and the campus began to go back to the era before the fashion president came. Suddenly no one was superior in dress. Suddenly there were no more answer keys to smuggle and students' grades dropped sharply. Even so, in any system, someone will still end up on top. She was a genius student who had won a million essay contests across the country. The essay princess, they called her. As if it never ran out, she always found ideas to write again, write, and create. She was always seen working over stacks of paper or a modern typewriter. All her essays were like windows to the world, covering every field of knowledge. Many said she had read thousands of books since she was small. Others said her parents began teaching her the exact sciences when she was a toddler. Those rumours kept spinning behind her back, and she never noticed because she was too busy writing.
If only someone knew who she really was. Before entering this campus, she was a fashion star in big magazines. Her life had revolved around clothes, and life seemed meaningless without other people's adoration. Then she panicked when she entered the fashion campus. She tried all sorts of ways and finally earned the title of essay princess. And now she graduated with the best grades in the whole country.
The essay princess already had followers from all over the world. How could she not? She started out as a star, and now she had the added edge of her talent for writing. So, in the end the princess decided to continue her career writing for the public. Book after book she published. Topics from politics to science, none were missed.
Behind all the fans popping up, spam emails from unknown senders kept piling up. Knowing what they contained, the princess was all the more set on ignoring them. The same went for the other side: the longer their emails went unanswered, the more determined they were to come for the essay princess. Until finally the princess's door was broken down by force and the princess was arrested on strong suspicion of plagiarism. Thousands of rumours about the books she had read. But in reality, thousands of journals she had copied. Now all of that turned into thousands of days in confinement. Legend has it that behind prison bars she went madder and madder because she had no mind of her own. She felt her life was empty because there was nothing left for her to copy. She decided to end her life behind bars, empty of praise from her fans.
Two graduated alumni caught up in cases. The students didn't know about any of this. They were too busy chasing the privilege to look their best and to be treated with honour by others. Grades and education were chased for the wrong reasons. This was the only procedure they knew. Find a way to get high numbers, then dress up, not chase a dream. Is that how low a dream has fallen?
Besides chasing grades and fixing their outward appearance, there was something else they learned. Like the importance of connections and privileges. Learning nothing from the situation, many kids then tried to get close to teachers to get perfect numbers on paper. But they did it by lowering the teachers' dignity with offers of money. Bribes and kickbacks many times over became the newest trend at this school. Until some other students who knew this fact considered it normal and didn't tell anyone. They thought these students, let's just call them the contractors, really did deserve it. That's how this problem became an open secret no one ever challenged.
Even so, you can't call it lucky or a pity. Not every student came from a good, high-class background. That's why delinquents, truants, and lazybones could dress with no manners and complete freedom. Clothes became an excuse for bad business and dirty politics. Once again we say it. How ridiculous.
While the students gave up their sleep to bring each other down with illusory numbers on their school reports, the contractors got full facilities on campus. Their lives were so calm. So naive that they knew no solution to any of life's problems other than money. Since they were small, they only had to do what their parents told them and got paid to spend it. So, while the other students' motivation sheets were filled with lists of clothes they would buy, only their sheets were painted with the Eiffel Tower and tall buildings in America. Of course, that too was on their parents' orders. How sad.
But it's true, their dreams came true. They achieved them like horses. They could go to neighbouring countries only as something to be ridden. As tools to be controlled, because their wealth was abundant but their brains were empty. Happy in their own foolishness. The first of them walked into his office, signed papers, and went home. The money kept coming in and that one year went smoothly. Until one day, a group of criminals met him in secret. The papers he had been signing all this time turned out to be debt papers with that criminal group. That day, a contractor disappeared without a trace. His family realised there was nothing they could do and could only hope. Legend has it that horrifying screams are heard every night at the place he was last seen. The longer it goes, the louder the voice. “That wasn't me. I don't know anything!” that's how the scream sounds every night. His ignorance swallowed him whole.
The other contractors' stories also ended badly. Just like the first one, they graduated with nothing. No achievements, no grades, no future. Every day they were just leeches on their parents. Some chose to repeat their schooling. Others went on to work and got positions in the name of money. That's how their lives became useless, nothing but the rotting trash of society. Living with the other leeches, only worshipping good names, appearance, and wealth that kept circling among them.
These students' cases were buried by the campus, hushed with papers inked in dollars. The dress rules were worshipped more and more and there was no effort to get rid of dress discrimination here. So, who here didn't go mad and wicked? How abnormal he must be. But there really was one.
That student was a champion in every field. Sports he won, and he was the fastest. Subjective art seemed like an open book to him. His writing moved everyone's heart. Not done with his achievements, he knew the exact sciences by heart too. He led campus organisations with ease. It seemed there was nothing in this world he couldn't do.
On the other hand, his cleverness brought out cunning and a huge ego in him. Every day he changed clothes. The talented one saw this situation as an advantage he could use. One day, he wore his olympiad team shirt to use sports facilities without paying. Another day, he secretly used his medal to steal books from the library in the name of the competition organisers. The very next day, he used his organisation jacket as an excuse for being late and skipping lectures. And so it went every day, his tricks always changing so no one would find out.
Until, on his graduation day, he was satisfied and got a job at one of the most famous companies in the world. Even so, his rank there wasn't high enough. And he couldn't get promoted either. A brilliant brain wasn't enough for him, because his boss always took advantage of his genius. Every genius idea he proposed was always claimed by someone else, and every mistake was dropped on him. It's a good thing he was smart, because the talented one managed to survive until now. But because of that too, his suffering lasted a long time. Time passed and passed, and into old age he stayed stuck in that position and couldn't move jobs. That's how the talented one got his karma, by being used.

blocks.text:
Si bertalenta ini mempunyai sahabat dekat yang bernasib tak jauh dengannya. Sang pekerja keras. Walau tak jenius, dirinya adalah manusia paling rajin yang pernah ditemukan. Tak ada rasa bosan dalam dirinya ketika mempelajari sesuatu. Hidupnya sangat menginspirasi dan menjadi teladan semua umat. Hanya satu kelemahannya. Mimpi.
Mimpi-mimpi yang dimiliki semua orang seakan tak berpihak pada dirinya. Dirinya selalu menyibukkan diri untuk membaca dan belajar. Benar-benar tak memberi waktu untuk sang pekerja keras rehat dan merefleksikan diri. Satu kata untuknya. Ia gila belajar. Saat makan, Ia membaca buku. Saat mandi, Ia mendengarkan radio pendidikan. Saat waktu tidur tiba, dirinya memilih untuk tidur seminimal mungkin dan melanjutkan menulis dan berkarya. Namun untuk apa semua itu?
Satu-satunya hal yang ia tahu adalah bagaimana ia hidup untuk mencari nilai-nilai di atas kertas. Sejak kecil, sang pekerja keras tidak pernah keluar dari lingkup kampus. Orang tuanya adalah seseorang yang selalu bekerja, seperti anaknya, dan tak pernah pulang. Mereka hanya meletakkan anaknya di kampus ini dengan bekal secukupnya. Selain untuk melanjutkan pendidikan, ia hidup untuk mengikuti tren busana di kampus itu. Hingga kembali tiba hari kelulusan. Lagi.
Sejarah terulang, si pekerja keras lulus dengan nilai terbaik. Lagi dan lagi. Namun, sudah dapat ditebak kemana dirinya akan melanjutkan karirnya. Ia akan terus belajar dan menambah ilmu. Belajar dan menciptakan karya-karya baru. Belajar dan menulis buku-buku untuk dipajang dirumahnya. Berprestasi untuk dirinya sendiri. Mereka simpan semua karya anak itu dalam sebuah ruang tertutup. Katanya karyanya terlalu berharga untuk ditunjukkan pada dunia. Lalu apa gunanya ia menggali ilmu? Sang pekerja keras juga tak tahu. Ia hanya tahu bahwa ia akan hidup untuk selalu ke penatu dengan gratis.
Tahun demi tahun. Abad berganti abad. Lulusan-lulusan kampus busana semakin patut untuk dicurigai. Kampus tak bisa lagi menahan tumpukan prasangka buruk dari publik. Rumor- rumor keburukan lulusan kampus ini sudah meluap menjadi pembicaraan masyarakat yang tak sadar telah menjadi fakta-fakta yang dipercaya. Semakin menumpuk pertanyaan-pertanyaan masyarakat mendorong lembaga-lembaga pendidikan untuk bergerak. Negara pun diam-diam mengirimkan mata-mata untuk menyelidiki. Dengan berbekal ketidaktahuan dan kepercayaan penuh kepada kampus favorit ini, mereka menyamar menjadi salah seorang mahasiswa di sana. Namun, dengan mudah mata-mata itu mendapatkan kebenarannya. Begitulah bagaimana tidak sampai satu hari mereka tinggal disana, mata-mata itu kembali keluar.
blocks.en:
The talented one had a close friend whose fate wasn't far from his. The hard worker. Though not a genius, he was the most diligent human ever found. There was no boredom in him when he was learning something. His life was so inspiring, a role model for everyone. Just one weakness. Dreams.
The dreams everyone else had never seemed to be on his side. He always kept himself busy reading and studying. Truly giving the hard worker no time to rest and reflect. One word for him. He was mad about studying. While eating, he read a book. While showering, he listened to educational radio. When bedtime came, he chose to sleep as little as possible and kept writing and creating. But what was all that for?
The only thing he knew was how to live to chase grades on paper. Since he was small, the hard worker had never left the campus grounds. His parents were people who were always working, like their child, and never came home. They just left their child at this campus with just enough to get by. Besides continuing his education, he lived to follow the fashion trends on that campus. Until graduation day came again. Again.
History repeated itself, the hard worker graduated with the best grades. Again and again. But it was easy to guess where he would take his career. He would keep studying and adding to his knowledge. Studying and creating new works. Studying and writing books to display in his home. Achieving for himself. They kept all the boy's works in a closed room. They said his work was too precious to show the world. Then what was the point of him digging for knowledge? The hard worker didn't know either. He only knew that he would live to always go to the laundry for free.
Year after year. Century after century. Graduates of the fashion campus grew more and more suspicious. The campus could no longer hold back the piles of bad assumptions from the public. Rumours about the bad deeds of this campus's graduates had overflowed into public talk that, without anyone noticing, had become facts people believed. The growing pile of public questions pushed educational institutions to act. The state, too, secretly sent spies to investigate. Armed with ignorance and full trust in this favourite campus, they disguised themselves as students there. But the spies found the truth easily. That's how, before even a day there, the spies came back out.

blocks.text:
“Sebentar, aku masih tidak yakin akan mengelak pernyataan ini. Biarkan aku memastikan sekali lagi.” Kata salah seorang dari mereka. Ketidakpercayaan mereka yang begitu besar semakin mendorong rasa penasaran dari dunia luar.
Satu minggu mereka disana, keluarlah mereka membawa selembar kertas bertuliskan presiden busana. Masyarakat sudah siap mendengarkan mata-mata itu membantah semua rumor buruk. Namun, fakta berkata sebaliknya.
“Tidak dapat dipercaya, selama ini kita hanya berimajinasi buruk terhadap kampus itu. Nyatanya kampus ini tidak memiliki masalah apa-apa. Normal-normal saja dari yang kami lihat. Kampus ini benar-benar cocok disebut kampus favorit nomor satu.”
“Lalu mengapa rumor itu tersebar?” jawab seorang hakim.
“Bagaimana tidak? Orang-orang sangatlah iri dan dengki, sebagaimana adanya sifat manusia. Kampus itu memiliki pendidikan yang sangat sempurna dan sesuai untuk negara kita. Sesungguhnya, kita, negara busana harus belajar dari kampus ini. Apa jadinya negara kita jika tidak dipimpin oleh anak-anak seperti mereka? Memang sudah seharusnya kita dipipimpin oleh sekelompok pemuja busana yang berprestasi.” Kata mata-mata itu terhadap pimpinannya, yaitu ia yang disebut presiden busana.
blocks.en:
“Wait, I'm still not sure I'll deny this statement. Let me make sure one more time.” Said one of them. Their huge disbelief pushed the outside world's curiosity even further.
After a week there, they came out carrying a sheet of paper with the words fashion president written on it. The public was ready to hear the spies refute all the bad rumours. But the facts said otherwise.
“Unbelievable, all this time we were only imagining bad things about that campus. In fact this campus has no problems at all. Perfectly normal from what we saw. This campus truly deserves to be called the number one favourite campus.”
“Then why did those rumours spread?” replied a judge.
“How could they not? People are so jealous and spiteful, as is human nature. That campus has a perfect education that suits our country. Truly, we, the fashion nation, must learn from this campus. What would become of our country if it weren't led by kids like them? It's only right that we are led by a group of high-achieving fashion worshippers.” Said the spy to their leader, the one called the fashion president.

posts.title: Ada Udang di Balik Pondok Madani (Refleksi Negeri 5 Menara)
posts.summary: Kisah-kisah Alif sebagai anak pesantren Pondok Mardani dimulai pada lembaran halaman ini. Pembacaan qanun, aturan tidak tertulis yang tidak boleh dilanggar menjadi…

blocks.text: Kisah-kisah Alif sebagai anak pesantren Pondok Mardani dimulai pada lembaran halaman ini. Pembacaan qanun, aturan tidak tertulis yang tidak boleh dilanggar menjadi perhatian utama saya ketika memasuki awal bagian. Hal ini seperti menunjukkan bagaimana Pondok Mardani mengenali sikap siswa pada sebuah aturan. Saya sendiri pernah melihat dan merasakan berada di sekolah atau suatu tempat yang berdiri di atas banyaknya aturan yang mengatur jalannya kegiatan. Peraturan yang terlalu banyak dan mengikat ini akhirnya tidak dapat diingat oleh seluruh anggota dan berakhir pada banyaknya pelanggaran yang terjadi.
blocks.en: Alif's stories as a student at the Pondok Mardani pesantren begin on these pages. The reading of the qanun, unwritten rules that must not be broken, became my main focus as I entered the start of this part. It's as if it shows how Pondok Mardani gets to know students' attitudes towards rules. I myself have seen and felt what it's like to be in a school or a place that stands on lots of rules governing how activities run. Too many binding rules like these end up impossible for all members to remember, and it ends in lots of violations.

blocks.text: Jika pada kasus Alif, peraturan tersebut dibacakan secara langsung dan memiliki jumlah yang masuk akal sehingga siswa dapat meresapinya dan memiliki motivasi untuk menghapalkannya. Seperti yang dikatakan oleh Kak Iskandar, ketua asrama
blocks.en: In Alif's case, the rules are read out directly and there's a reasonable number of them, so students can take them in and have the motivation to memorise them. As Kak Iskandar, the head of the dorm, says

blocks.text: “Akhi. Dengarkan baik-baik. Kita tidak mau membuat peraturan tertulis banyak-banyak, lalu kemudian dilupakan dan tidak diterapkan. Qanun ini maksudnya supaya apa yang disebutkan, dilaksanakan bersama. Memang tidak ada pengulangan karena harapannnya semua orang mencatat dalam hati masing-masing dan siap melaksanakannya.”
blocks.en: “Akhi. Listen carefully. We don't want to make lots of written rules that then get forgotten and never applied. The point of this qanun is that whatever is said, we carry out together. There's no repeating, because the hope is that everyone writes it down in their own heart and is ready to carry it out.”

blocks.text: Atas basis tersebut pun, sekolah dapat lebih tertata karena siswanya tertib dan penegak aturan dapat dengan mudah mengatasi jika adanya pelanggaran. Bahkan, hal yang membuat saya kagum adalah bagaimana selanjutnya disebutkan alasan dari adanya peraturan-peraturan itu ketika Alif bertanya.
blocks.en: On that basis too, the school can be more orderly because its students are disciplined, and those enforcing the rules can easily deal with any violations. What even amazed me is how the reasons behind those rules are then explained when Alif asks.

blocks.text: Menurut sebuah artikel yang memiliki tema “ Healthy Business, Healthy Employees”, terlalu banyaknya aturan akan memberikan efek buruk pada produktivitas karyawannya. Hal ini berlaku pula pada sebuah instansi Pendidikan. Memang untuk mendidik, namun apakah hal ini tidak membantu siswa untuk berani berkreativitas jika peraturan terlalu mengikat? Memiliki terlalu banyak aturan dapat membuat siswa merasa tidak dipercaya oleh sekolah dan pendapat mereka tidak memiliki bobot apa pun di sekolah. Artikel lain mengatakan bahwa terlalu banyak peraturan juga dapat menghambat rasa ingin tahu siswa. Oleh sebab itu, saya sangat menyukai bagaimana adanya sistem qanun ini pada pesantren Pondok Mardani.
blocks.en: According to an article themed “Healthy Business, Healthy Employees”, too many rules have a bad effect on employee productivity. This applies to educational institutions too. Sure, it's meant to educate, but won't it keep students from daring to be creative if the rules are too binding? Having too many rules can make students feel the school doesn't trust them and that their opinions carry no weight at school. Another article says that too many rules can also hold back students' curiosity. That's why I really like this qanun system at the Pondok Mardani pesantren.

blocks.text: Selain itu, dalam pelaksanaan selanjutnya dari qanun, siswa Pondok Madani dipercaya sendiri untuk menjunjung norma-norma dan peraturan lain yang sudah menjadi dasar dan selayaknya dilakukan. Seperti peraturan tentang kupon makan, hormat kepada yang lebih tua, sholat tepat waktu, dan lain-lain. Walaupun kehidupan anak pesantren di novel ini menjadi terlihat sangat padat dan tegas, adanya peraturan-peraturan tersebut memiliki dasar alasan yang jelas dan hasilnya diceritakan berdampak pada siswa.
blocks.en: Besides that, in carrying out the qanun afterwards, Pondok Madani students are trusted on their own to uphold the norms and other rules that are basic and simply the right thing to do. Like the rules about meal coupons, respecting elders, praying on time, and so on. Even though the life of pesantren students in this novel looks very packed and strict, those rules have clear reasons behind them, and the results are shown to have an impact on the students.

blocks.text: Sistem di pesantren Pondok Madani yang saya harapkan juga ada di pendidikan adalah metode Jasus. Metode jasus ini benar adanya untuk membangkitkan semangat aware kepada masalah di masyarakat sekitar. Sulitnya penegakan aturan kini telah merajalela, tidak hanya pada lingkup kecil seperti sekolah, namun juga pada lingkup besar seperti negara bahkan dunia.
blocks.en: A system at the Pondok Madani pesantren that I wish existed in education too is the Jasus method. The jasus method truly works to spark a spirit of being aware of problems in the surrounding community. Rules being hard to enforce is now rampant, not only in small spheres like schools, but also in big ones like countries, even the world.

blocks.text: Metode jasus menurut saya dapat mendidik anak untuk selalu rajin menepati aturan dan tidak takut menegakkan kebenaran. Sehingga di masa depan pun anak berani menegur dan tegas terhadap orang yang melanggar peraturan. Sudah menjadi rahasia umum, telah banyak sekali penyelewengan peraturan karena yang melawan akan dibungkam atau tergoda suapan yang bernilai besar. Bahkan anak-anak di sekolah pun tidak terhindar dari kebiasaan seperti ini. Secara tidak langsung siswa akan membenci kawannya yang berani memberi kritik dan menegur.
blocks.en: In my opinion, the jasus method can teach kids to always diligently follow the rules and not be afraid to stand up for what's right. So that in the future, too, kids will dare to call out and be firm with people who break the rules. It's an open secret that rules get bent all the time, because those who fight back get silenced or tempted by big bribes. Even kids at school can't escape habits like this. Indirectly, students end up hating the classmate who dares to criticise and call them out.

blocks.text: Kemudian tidak hanya jasus keamanan, ada juga jasus Bahasa di Pondok Mardani untuk mendorong siswa untuk dapat menguasai Bahasa asing, yaitu Bahasa Inggris dan Bahasa Arab. Jasus Bahasa ini juga diharapkan dapat diterapkan di instansi pendidikan lainnya di Indonesia. Seperti kata sebuah istilah dalam Bahasa Inggris “Fake it till you make it”. Paksakan itu hingga kalian mencapainya. Seperti yang Alif rasakan yaitu ketika dia awalnya sangat merasa terbebani dengan perlunya penggunaan Bahasa asing dalam kehidupannya. Namun, suatu saat, secara tidak sadar Alif sudah bisa membentuk kalimat lengkap dan menggunakan Bahasa asing tersebut sehari-hari.
blocks.en: And not just the security jasus, there's also a language jasus at Pondok Mardani to push students to master foreign languages, namely English and Arabic. I hope this language jasus can also be applied in other educational institutions in Indonesia. Like the English saying, “Fake it till you make it”. Force it until you get there. Just like what Alif felt when at first he felt very burdened by having to use foreign languages in his life. But one day, without even realising it, Alif could already form full sentences and use those foreign languages every day.

blocks.text: Tidak hanya dalam hal Bahasa, bab-bab ini juga kembali menunjukkan pembelajaran siswa yang sangat mengglobal. Padahal sesuai perhitungan saya, latar waktu cerita Alif ini sekitar tahun 1987-1991, tahun dimana komunikasi dan teknologi belum berkembang pesat di Indonesia. Kenyataan ini memutarbalikkan pemikiran saya di awal cerita, ketika Alif juga berpikir sekolah pesantren tidak sebaik sekolah negeri. Sekolah pesantren ini justru sangat luar biasa mendidik semua aspek dalam anak, yaitu kedisiplinan, ilmu, dan agama yang menjadi hal penting di Indonesia. Deskripsi dalam buku ini menunjukkan bahwa pendidikan yang terbaik dapat diterima oleh siapapun walau dihalangi banyaknya keterbatasan ekonomi yang banyak dideskripsikan oleh penulis pada Alif dan teman-temannya. Semua ini sesuai tujuan 4 SDG : Memastikan pendidikan yang inklusif dan berkualitas setara, juga mendukung kesempatan belajar seumur hidup bagi semua. Hal ini banyak ditunjukkan mulai dari pembelajaran dan ekstrakurikuler anak yang sangat beragam. Kemudian juga dari buku-buku bacaan Raja seperti Oxford Dictionary of Current Idiomatic English hingga buku yang dibawakan Ustad Salman untuk menjadi referensi lain bagi siswa untuk belajar.
blocks.en: Not only in language, these chapters again show how very global the students' learning is. And yet by my calculation, Alif's story is set around 1987-1991, years when communication and technology hadn't developed much in Indonesia. This fact turned around what I thought at the start of the story, when Alif also thought a pesantren wasn't as good as a state school. This pesantren actually does an extraordinary job of educating every aspect of a child: discipline, knowledge, and religion, which matter so much in Indonesia. The descriptions in this book show that the best education can be received by anyone, even when held back by the many economic limitations the author describes for Alif and his friends. All of this fits SDG 4: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. This is shown a lot, starting with the children's very diverse lessons and extracurriculars. Then also from Raja's books like the Oxford Dictionary of Current Idiomatic English, to the books Ustad Salman brings in as other references for students to learn from.

blocks.text: “Malam ini tidak ada yang baca buku pelajaran. Tapi saya akan bacakan kepada kalian potongan Mutiara kehidupan tokoh-tokoh ini,” katanya sambil memamerkan buku “Mandela: The Biography”, “BJ Habibie, Mutiara dari Timur”, “Bung Hatta, Pribadinya dalam Kenangan”, “Marthin Luther King, Jr: Stride Toward Freedom”, dan “Mohammed, the Man of Allah”.
blocks.en: “Tonight nobody reads textbooks. But I will read you snippets from the pearls of life of these figures,” he said, showing off the books “Mandela: The Biography”, “BJ Habibie, Mutiara dari Timur”, “Bung Hatta, Pribadinya dalam Kenangan”, “Marthin Luther King, Jr: Stride Toward Freedom”, and “Mohammed, the Man of Allah”.

blocks.text: Selain dalam aspek pendidikan, bab ini kembali menunjukkan keberagaman budaya khususnya dari daerah asal Alif dan teman-temannya. Pada sela kisah kehidupan Alif di pesantren, diselipkan carita tradisi budaya Marosok yang unik secara detail. Ada juga kelucuan dari Atang yang masih suka menggunakan Bahasa Sunda hingga perjalanan kecil mereka di Ponorogo. Namun dibalik itu, Alif dan teman-temannya dapat saling memahami dan menjalin pertemanan yang kuat.
blocks.en: Besides education, this chapter again shows cultural diversity, especially from the hometowns of Alif and his friends. In between the stories of Alif's life at the pesantren, the unique Marosok cultural tradition is slipped in, told in detail. There's also the humour of Atang, who still likes using Sundanese, right up to their little trip to Ponorogo. But behind it all, Alif and his friends are able to understand each other and build a strong friendship.
