blocks.text: Terkadang kita menyebut sesuatu itu berharga tanpa berpikir. Orang atau mungkin mahkluk lain selalu melihat hal yang berharga dalam bentuk yang berbeda. Begitu pula pada seorang pria yang sedang berdiri di toko sepedanya. Di hadapan ribuan orang perwakilan dari petinggi-petinggi negara, artis papan atas, kalangan rakyat menengah, hingga pendatang dan orang penting dari benua seberang, Ia tetap berdiri mematung dengan tangan kanannya memegang setang sepeda onthel untuk menunjukkan kepemilikannya. Bukti kegilaan dunia oleh seorang pria bermula sejak beberapa pekan lalu.
blocks.en: Sometimes we call something precious without thinking. People, or maybe other creatures, always see precious things in different forms. So it was with a man standing in his bicycle shop. Before thousands of people, envoys of the country's top officials, A-list celebrities, ordinary middle-class folk, even newcomers and important people from the continent across the sea, he stood frozen like a statue, his right hand on the handlebar of an old onthel bicycle to show it was his. The proof of how one man drove the world mad began a few weeks earlier.

blocks.text: Hari itu, sebuah toko baru dibuka di atas tanah kecil bekas pergusuran rumah warga. Dengan ukuran yang tak lebih lebar dari lebar sebuah mobil sedan dan satu meter lebih panjang untuk masuknya sebuah sepeda, toko ini cukup mengundang rasa penasaran dari tetangga sesama pemilik toko di blok. Sudah lima tahun lebih bangunan toko itu kosong dan kini tiba-tiba muncul sebuah toko sepeda di tengah pusat perdagangan modern tengah kota.
blocks.en: That day, a new shop opened on a small plot of land where people's houses had once been torn down. No wider than a sedan and just a metre longer to fit a bicycle inside, the shop stirred plenty of curiosity among the neighbouring shop owners on the block. The building had stood empty for more than five years, and now, suddenly, a bicycle shop appeared in the middle of the city's modern trading centre.

blocks.text: Akhirnya, terkalahkan oleh rasa penasaran, para tetangga tersebut bergantian berlalu-lalang di depan toko untuk sesekali melirik-lirik ke dalam. Puas bermain mata, mereka berkumpul kembali.
blocks.en: In the end, beaten by curiosity, the neighbours took turns strolling back and forth in front of the shop, sneaking glances inside. Once they'd had their fill of peeking, they gathered again.

blocks.text: “Lihatkah engkau? Ia hanya memiliki satu sepeda onthel di dalam toko.” Ujar seorang pemilik bar di area tersebut.
blocks.en: “Did you see? He only has one onthel bicycle in the shop.” said a bar owner from the area.

blocks.text: “Oh. Sudah pasti betapa mahalnya sepeda onthel tersebut.” Timpal saudagar rokok yang tokonya berada di sudut kota.
blocks.en: “Oh. That onthel bicycle must be terribly expensive, then.” chimed in a cigarette merchant whose shop sat on the corner of town.

blocks.text: “Mengapa engkau begitu yakin? Bukankah itu sangat aneh? Biar aku tanyakan.” Setelah mengatakan demikian, seorang polisi mendatangi sang pria pemilik toko. Untuk mendapatkan sepeda itu, tak banyak yang dibutuhkan sang pria. Ia hanya berkata,
blocks.en: “Why are you so sure? Isn't it very strange? Let me ask.” Having said so, a policeman went up to the man who owned the shop. To get the bicycle, the man didn't ask for much. He only said,

blocks.text: “Berikanlah aku hal berharga sebagai barang tukar untuk sepedaku karena dialah yang akan membawa kalian ke puncak kejayaan.”
blocks.en: “Give me something precious in exchange for my bicycle, for it is the one that will carry you to the peak of glory.”

blocks.text: Terheranlah seluruh tetangga dan orang-orang yang ikut berkumpul disitu. Beberapa menganggapnya gila atas pernyataannya tersebut. Beberapa yang lain sibuk memikirkan hal apakah yang dapat sang pria anggap berharga? Mendengar hal itu, seorang pedagang pasar datang dan menawar. Dengan rupa yang masih terlihat belum pernah dikayuh itu, sepeda onthel tersebut ditawar dengan harga 500 lembar uang. Sang pria tak bergeming dan dengan halus mulutnya mengucapkan tidak.
blocks.en: All the neighbours and the people gathered there were bewildered. Some thought he was mad for saying such a thing. Others were busy wondering what on earth the man would consider precious. Hearing this, a market trader came forward and made an offer. Looking as if it had never once been pedalled, the onthel bicycle was offered 500 notes. The man didn't budge, and his mouth gently said no.

blocks.text: Selanjutnya, melihat pedagang pasar itu ditolak, datanglah pemilik sebuah market besar untuk menawar dengan harga dua kali lipat. 1000 lembar uang. Tetapi, kata yang sama terucap di mulut sang pria. Tidak.
blocks.en: Next, seeing the market trader turned down, the owner of a big supermarket came to offer double. 1000 notes. But the same word came out of the man's mouth. No.

blocks.text: Menyaksikan dua tawaran tersebut ditolak, maka, semakin berhargalah sepeda itu di mata para warga. Orang- orang di kota itu mulai menawarkan harganya masing-masing demi mendapatkan sepeda itu. Namun, kata “tidak” selalu keluar dari bibir sang pria. Hingga berita ini terdengar oleh seorang pemilik toko sepeda terbesar di kota. Pantas saja akhir-akhir ini peminat sepeda tidak mendatangi tokonya. Ia kemudian bersumpah akan menemukan alasannya dan mengakhirinya. Akhirnya, pemilik toko sepeda terbesar di kota pun datang menawarkan untuk bertukar dengan sebuah sepeda, sepeda keluaran terbaru yang baru saja diimpor. Tetapi, tetap saja kata yang sama terulang untuk menandakan penolakan sang pria.
blocks.en: Having watched both offers refused, the bicycle grew all the more precious in the townspeople's eyes. People across the city began naming their own prices to get it. But the word “no” always left the man's lips. Until the news reached the owner of the biggest bicycle shop in the city. No wonder bicycle buyers hadn't been coming to his shop lately. He swore he would find the reason and put an end to it. At last, the owner of the biggest bicycle shop in the city came too, offering to trade a bicycle, the very latest model, freshly imported. But still the same word was repeated, the man's refusal.

blocks.text: Merasa kesal, pemilik toko sepeda terbesar di kota itu menendang sepeda impornya dan kembali dengan jumlah sepeda yang lebih. Sepuluh sepeda dengan kualitas teratas itu ditawarkannya. Gelengan kembali dilakukan oleh sang pria. Sang pemilik toko sepeda itu akhirnya menendang kembali seluruh sepedanya karena marah dan kesal. Begitu pula keesokan harinya dan seterusnya, jumlah sepeda yang ditawarkan untuk barter terus meningkat dua kali lipat dari hari kemarin.
blocks.en: Annoyed, the owner of the biggest bicycle shop in the city kicked his imported bicycle and came back with more bicycles. Ten bicycles of the finest quality, he offered. The man shook his head again. The shop owner ended up kicking all his bicycles out of anger and frustration. And so it went the next day, and the next, the number of bicycles offered in trade doubling from the day before.

blocks.text: Hingga akhirnya tiba pada sepeda terakhir miliknya, Ia tendang untuk meluapkan emosi karena penolakan. Kemudian, tersadarlah Ia atas apa yang sudah dilakukannya. Karena emosinya, Ia berakhir tak memiliki apa-apa di hidupnya. Terceritalah, sesaat setelah itu, utang-utang datang melilit dirinya dan tak ada keluarga yang ingin membantu orang itu. Orang yang selalu memperhitungkan harta ketika mereka butuh bantuan. Kini, Ia mengakhiri hidupnya sendiri untuk lari dari utang yang mengikat raganya. Namun, tidak ada yang tahu akan nasibnya sekarang yang masih terlilit utang yang mengikat jiwanya.
blocks.en: Until at last it came to his very last bicycle, and he kicked it to vent his rage at being refused. Then he realised what he had done. Because of his temper, he ended up with nothing in his life. The story goes that soon after, debts came and wrapped themselves around him, and no family wanted to help him. The man who always counted his wealth whenever they needed help. Now, he ended his own life to escape the debts binding his body. But no one knows his fate now, still tangled in the debts binding his soul.

blocks.text: Para warga melihat pemilik toko sepeda terbesar di kota itu menawarkan seluruh kepemilikannya untuk sebuah sepeda onthel dan berakhir mengenaskan. Bukannya mengakhiri hal ini, para warga justru semakin terkagum dan memuja-muja sepeda onthel tersebut. Tidak bisa tinggal diam, berita mengenai sepeda ini tersebar ke berbagai daerah dan terus menyebar. Namanya juga dari orang ke orang dan tidak ada yang melarang untuk melebih-lebihkan berita tersebut. Ada yang mengatakan sepeda itu dahulu merupakan sepeda onthel pertama di dunia. Lalu yang lain mengelak dan mengatakan sepeda ini adalah sepeda milik seorang raja. Seorang ksatria palsu mengatakan ini adalah sepeda yang memberimu kesaktian dan kekuatan. Dari bibir ke telinga berita itu selalu berubah. Hingga akhirnya berita yang mengatakan sepeda ini akan membawa harta sampai di telinga seorang saudagar terkaya di pulau.
blocks.en: The townspeople saw the owner of the biggest bicycle shop in the city offer everything he owned for an onthel bicycle and end up wretched. Instead of putting an end to this, the people were even more amazed and began to worship the onthel bicycle. It couldn't stay quiet, the news about the bicycle spread to other regions and kept spreading. That's what happens when it passes from person to person and no one forbids exaggerating it. Some said the bicycle had once been the first onthel bicycle in the world. Then others denied it and said it belonged to a king. A fake knight said it was a bicycle that gives you magic powers and strength. From lips to ears the news kept changing. Until finally, the version saying this bicycle would bring riches reached the ears of the richest merchant on the island.

blocks.text: Menurut cerita, dahulu kala ada seorang saudagar yang baik hati. Karena kemurahan hatinya tersebut, akhirnya rakyat memilihnya untuk menjadi perwakilan di hadapan pemerintah. Tidak seperti pejabat lainnya, Ia tetap memperjuangkan keadilan dan tanggung jawab kepada orang yang memilihnya. Sayang, jabatannya terlalu rendah untuk didengar. Sedangkan Ia sendiri sadar, Ia tak akan pernah naik jika tangannya tidak kotor. Teriakan rakyat untuk keadilan terus mendorongnya untuk berbuat sesuatu. Rakyat yang naif, pikirnya. Akhirnya desakan itu mendorongnya untuk memanjat ke atas dengan mengotori tangannya. Ia berjanji ketika sudah di puncak, Ia akan membersihkan tangannya kembali, bahkan membersihkan seluruh negeri dari pemerintahan yang kotor.
blocks.en: As the story goes, long ago there was a kind-hearted merchant. Because of his generosity, the people chose him to be their representative before the government. Unlike the other officials, he kept fighting for justice and his responsibility to those who had chosen him. Sadly, his position was too low to be heard. And he knew himself, he would never rise if his hands stayed clean. The people's cries for justice kept pushing him to do something. Naive people, he thought. In the end that pressure pushed him to climb upward by dirtying his hands. He promised that once he reached the top, he would clean his hands again, and even clean the whole country of its dirty government.

blocks.text: Demikianlah, Ia menjadi pejabat di tingkat predator tertinggi. Walau begitu Ia tetap memegang janjinya untuk membersihkan tangannya. Sayang beribu sayang lagi, Ia juga tetap kukuh memegang tekadnya untuk terus menunda janji. Besok. Besok saja. Masih ada besok. Begitulah pikirnya. Hingga saat ini janji manisnya itu berakhir mengotori seluruh negeri. Ia melihat dirinya sebagai orang baik, mengabaikan derita rakyat yang menjadi makanannya. Jabatannya kini, Ia manfaatkan sebaik-baiknya. Benar-benar sebaik-baiknya untuk membangun perusahaannya menjadi semakin besar. Ketika telah berhasil menyeret perusahaannya ke tingkat tertinggi, Ia mundur dari jabatannya dan meninggalkan kotorannya.
blocks.en: And so, he became an official at the very top of the food chain. Even so, he still held on to his promise to clean his hands. A thousand times sadly, he also held firmly to his resolve to keep putting that promise off. Tomorrow. Just tomorrow. There's still tomorrow. That was how he thought. Until now that sweet promise of his has ended up dirtying the whole country. He saw himself as a good man, ignoring the suffering of the people who had become his food. His position now, he used to the fullest. Truly to the fullest, to make his company bigger and bigger. Once he had dragged his company to the very top, he resigned from his post and left his filth behind.

blocks.text: Ia yang menganggap dirinya baik itu datang ke toko sepeda dan merasa sangat layak mendapatkannya. “Wahai, penjual sepeda. Berapakah Kau inginkan untuk menukarnya dengan sepedamu itu? Katakanlah! Aku akan beri semua.” Katanya dengan berpikir remeh seberapa kecil harta yang harus Ia keluarkan untuk sang pria penjual sepeda.
blocks.en: This man who considered himself good came to the bicycle shop feeling very much deserving of it. “O, bicycle seller. How much do you want in exchange for that bicycle of yours? Speak! I'll give it all.” he said, scoffing to himself at how little wealth he'd have to spend on the bicycle-selling man.

blocks.text: “Aku hanya perlu hal berharga. Bagiku dan bukan bagimu.” Jawab sang pria.
blocks.en: “I only need something precious. To me, and not to you.” the man replied.

blocks.text: Saat itu juga, saudagar itu menghujani toko sepeda sang pria dengan uang dan hartanya. Timbunan pertama tidak diterima. Timbunan kedua tetap tidak. Setiap timbunan yang berjumlah selalu berkali-kali lipat lebih banyak selalu dijawab dengan gelengan kepala sang pria. Timbunan harta ke-77 berakhir dengan gelengan tidak pula. Hartanya pun habis. Semuanya memenuhi toko sang pria dan menimbun jalanan di kota. Ia frustasi karena tawarannya yg tak pernah ditolak itu selalu ditolak mentah-mentah oleh sang pria. Akhirnya, Ia menawarkan harta terakhir miliknya, busananya. Ia yakin sang pria akan menukarnya dengan semua hartanya ini dan memberikan sepedanya yang pastinya akan membawa harta lebih yang pantas baginya. Tak terduga baginya, sang pria menolak kembali hartanya itu.
blocks.en: Right then and there, the merchant showered the man's bicycle shop with his money and riches. The first heap was not accepted. The second heap still no. Every heap, each always many times bigger than the last, was answered with a shake of the man's head. The 77th heap of riches also ended in a shake of no. And then his riches ran out. All of it filled the man's shop and buried the streets of the city. He was frustrated because his offers, which had never been refused, were always flatly refused by the man. Finally, he offered the last thing he owned, his clothes. He was sure the man would trade all these riches and hand over the bicycle that would surely bring him the greater fortune he deserved. Unexpectedly for him, the man refused his riches once again.

blocks.text: Tak memiliki apapun untuk ditawarkan lagi, akhirnya saudagar itu meminta pelayannya untuk mengumpulkan kembali hartanya untuk dibawa pulang. Nahas, pelayan itu tidak cukup bodoh untuk kembali diperbudak, maka, ketika mengetahui semua harta tuannya berada di situ. Satu-persatu dari mereka segera memunguti harta milik tuannya. Melihat hal itu, warga ikut memunguti uang yang sebenarnya memang milik mereka. Saudagar kaya seketika menjadi miskin, kasut pun tidak punya. Karena terlalu terkejut akan nasibnya, Ia berakhir terkena serangan jantung. Konon katanya, dokter yang merawatnya memiliki dendam kepadanya. Perawatan yang seharusnya dilakukan kepadanya selalu ditunda. Besok. Besok saja. Masih ada besok. Begitulah kata dokter itu setiap hari. Tanpa bisa berkata apa-apa, saudagar itu hanya bisa menahan sakit.
blocks.en: With nothing left to offer, the merchant finally told his servants to gather his riches back up to take home. Unluckily for him, the servants weren't foolish enough to be enslaved again, so, once they knew all their master's riches were right there. One by one, they quickly picked up their master's riches. Seeing this, the townspeople joined in picking up the money that had really been theirs all along. The rich merchant became poor in an instant, not even a pair of sandals to his name. Too shocked by his fate, he ended up having a heart attack. Rumour has it, the doctor who treated him held a grudge against him. The treatment he should have received was always postponed. Tomorrow. Just tomorrow. There's still tomorrow. That's what the doctor said every day. Unable to say a word, the merchant could only bear the pain.

blocks.text: Bertambahlah penawaran dari orang-orang besar, berkuasa, dan terkenal setelah mendengar kisah mengenai sepeda onthel tersebut. Setelah mendapat harta yang begitu besar, warga semakin memuja-muja sepeda tersebut. Benar-benar sepeda yang membawa keberuntungan. Sepeda itu mulai menjadi pusat kota dan simbol dari kota.
blocks.en: More offers poured in from big, powerful, and famous people after hearing the tale of the onthel bicycle. Having received such great riches, the townspeople worshipped the bicycle even more. Truly a bicycle that brings good luck. The bicycle began to become the centre of the city and the symbol of the city.

blocks.text: Selain mengundang pemujaan, sepeda itu juga mengundang niat jahat. Di suatu malam, seorang perampok datang untuk merampok sepeda itu. Dengan mudahnya ia mendapatkan sepeda yang hanya diletakkan saja di dalam toko tanpa pintu yang terkunci. Merasakan kemenangan, Ia menuntun sepeda dengan begitu senang. Walau begitu, aneh jika perampok itu tidak merasa curiga. Bagaimana mungkin sepeda yang menggemparkan dunia ini didapatkannya dengan sangat mudah?
blocks.en: Besides drawing worship, the bicycle also drew wicked intentions. One night, a robber came to rob the bicycle. So easily he got the bicycle, which was simply left inside the shop with no locked door. Feeling victorious, he wheeled the bicycle away, so very happy. Even so, it would be strange if the robber didn't feel suspicious. How could this bicycle that had shaken the world be his so easily?

blocks.text: Tiba-tiba, Ia mendengar bisik-bisik orang diujung gang. “Aku dengar sepeda itu dijaga oleh pasukan jin. Siapa yang berani mengambilnya akan langsung mati jiwanya setelah 10 menit?” kata seorang ibu kepada tetangganya sambil menjemur pakaian. Takutlah perampok itu setelah mendengarnya. Benar saja, ketika Ia menoleh ke sebelah kanannya, sepasukan mahkluk yang tak dikenalinya sedang melihat ke arahnya. Terbirit-birit, Ia segera menaiki sepeda onthel itu dan mengayuh menjauhi tempat itu. Dengan berantakan dan terjatuh-jatuh, Ia terus mengayuh hingga berjam-jam untuk menghindari mahkluk yang Ia duga adalah jin. Para jin itu tidak pernah berhasil menangkapnya. Namun, juga tidak membiarkan perampok lolos. Seolah-olah itulah yang mereka rencanakan. Akhirnya, Ia terhenti di depan toko sepeda sang pria lagi. Berpuluh-puluh mahkluk jin juga berhenti di balik gedung sekitar lalu menguliti sang perampok dengan matanya. Sang perampok kemudian berlari dan terjatuh-jatuh karena terlalu takut, tentu saja melupakan hasil curiannya di depan toko.
blocks.en: Suddenly, he heard people whispering at the end of the alley. “I heard that bicycle is guarded by an army of jinn. Whoever dares take it, their soul will die in 10 minutes?” said a woman to her neighbour while hanging out the laundry. The robber was frightened after hearing it. Sure enough, when he turned to his right, a troop of creatures he didn't recognise were looking straight at him. In a panic, he jumped on the onthel bicycle and pedalled away from that place. Wobbling and falling again and again, he kept pedalling for hours to escape the creatures he guessed were jinn. The jinn never managed to catch him. But they never let the robber get away either. As if that was exactly what they had planned. Finally, he stopped in front of the man's bicycle shop again. Dozens of jinn stopped too, behind the buildings around, and skinned the robber with their eyes. The robber then ran, tripping and falling because he was too scared, and of course forgot his loot in front of the shop.

blocks.text: Keesokan harinya, terpampang sebuah berita konyol di halaman depan koran. Tempat berita utama diletakkan, yang tentunya masih di bawah berita sepeda onthel sang pria. Dituliskan pada berita bahwa terdapat orang gila yang berlari-lari tanpa alasan dan terus berteriak “Maafkan aku. Aku mohon. Maaf.” Itulah alasan dari keributan tadi malam pukul 12.10 . Setelah membaca koran pagi tersebut, sang pria pemilik toko sepeda tersenyum dan mengeluarkan sepeda onthel nya yang belum berpindah tempat sejak kemarin sore.
blocks.en: The next day, a ridiculous story was splashed across the front page of the newspaper. The spot where the headline goes, still below the news about the man's onthel bicycle, of course. The story said there was a madman running around for no reason, shouting over and over “Forgive me. I beg you. Sorry.” That was the reason for the commotion last night at 12.10. After reading the morning paper, the man who owned the bicycle shop smiled and brought out his onthel bicycle, which hadn't moved from its spot since the afternoon before.

blocks.text: Antrean untuk menawar sepeda itu masih panjang. Siapapun yang mengantre selalu berakhir pada tolakan. Sepeda onthel itu seakan-akan menjadi barang paling mulia di dunia. Semua mengorbankan sesuatu untuk ditukar dengan sepeda onthel itu. Seorang wanita mengorbankan tubuhnya untuk ditukar. Seorang lelaki menjual hatinya untuk ditukar. Seorang ayah memberi anaknya untuk ditukar. Seorang pelukis memberi tangannya untuk ditukar. Seorang pelari memberi kakinya untuk ditukar. Begitulah semua menawarkan hal paling berharga di hidupnya untuk sepeda onthel itu. Namun, tetap saja sang pria berkata tidak untuk menolak penawaran mereka dan semua berakhir mengenaskan untuk penawar.
blocks.en: The queue to bid on the bicycle was still long. Whoever queued always ended up refused. The onthel bicycle seemed to become the most exalted thing in the world. Everyone sacrificed something to trade for that onthel bicycle. A woman sacrificed her body to trade. A man sold his heart to trade. A father gave his child to trade. A painter gave his hands to trade. A runner gave his legs to trade. That was how everyone offered the most precious thing in their lives for that onthel bicycle. But still the man said no to refuse their offers, and it all ended wretchedly for the bidders.

blocks.text: Hingga, tiba di ujung antrean, seorang anak kecil ikut mengantre. Ia mengira orang-orang ini mengantre hanya untuk membeli sebuah sepeda biasa. Walaupun memang benar sepeda itu adalah sepeda onthel biasa.
blocks.en: Until, at the end of the queue, a little child joined the line. He thought these people were queuing just to buy an ordinary bicycle. Although it was true, that bicycle was just an ordinary onthel bicycle.

blocks.text: “Bolehkan aku membeli sepeda ini? Bisakah aku mendapatkannya dengan uang segini. Kumohon, aku membutuhkannya untuk mengantar adikku ke sekolah hari ini.” Tanya anak kecil itu dengan tangannya yang menunjukkan uang 1 lembar. Warga di sekitar tertawa. Lalu benarlah pemikiran mereka, sang pria menggeleng pula. Namun, untuk alasan yang berbeda.
blocks.en: “Can I buy this bicycle? Can I get it with this much money. Please, I need it to take my little sister to school today.” the little child asked, his hand holding out a single note. The people around laughed. And just as they thought, the man shook his head too. But for a different reason.

blocks.text: “Tidak perlu membayar, nak. Ambillah saja sepeda itu.” Sebelum warga maju untuk protes, sang pria melanjutkan. “Lagipula sepeda ini sudah selesai melakukan tugasnya bagiku. Sekarang dunia sudah bersih. Lalu, bagimu, gunakanlah sepeda ini untuk melakukan tugasnya.”
blocks.en: “No need to pay, kid. Just take the bicycle.” Before the people could step forward to protest, the man went on. “Besides, this bicycle has finished its task for me. Now the world is clean. And for you, use this bicycle to do its task.”

blocks.text: Segera setelah itu anak kecil tersebut segera berterimakasih dan mengayuh sepeda membiarkan tatapan tak percaya dari seluruh dunia di punggungnya. Akhirnya, mereka semua menyadari semua tindakan sang pria dan mulai merenungkannya. Sama seperti yang terjadi lima tahun lalu, ditutuplah kembali toko tersebut. Andai manusia ingat, barang terbaru akan selalu datang ketika manusia mengulangi dosa mereka kembali.
blocks.en: Right after that the little child quickly said thank you and pedalled off, leaving the whole world's disbelieving stares on his back. At last, they all understood everything the man had done and began to reflect on it. Just like what happened five years ago, the shop was closed once more. If only humans remembered, the newest thing will always come when humans repeat their sins again.

blocks.text: Cerpen oleh : Felicia Tiffany H

en.title: If Only You Remembered
en.summary: Sometimes we call something precious without thinking. People, or maybe other creatures, always see precious things in different forms. So it was with…
